CT561 Paper-Based Topic Guide

Graphical and Euler Integration

A recent-paper core: the same three-part integration question appears in 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26, and closely matches earlier papers.

What the recent paper asks

  • Part (a) [12]: draw the stock-flow model including net flow, calculate net flow, then use graphical integration to plot the stock and explain each behaviour mode.
  • Part (b) [5]: describe Euler's method and assumptions; explain when forward Euler over- or underestimates the stock, supported by a short calculation.
  • Part (c) [8]: use Euler with the stated DT, normally a deliberately large time step.

References: 2023/24 Q4(a-c), 2024/25 Q4(a-c), 2025/26 Q1(a-c). Older versions: 2018/19 Q1 and 2021/22 Q4.

Part (a): graphical integration

Draw a rectangle for the stock, pipes for the named inflow and outflow, and an auxiliary: Net Flow = Inflow - Outflow. Then write Stock = INTEG(Net Flow, Initial Stock).

  1. Calculate or sketch net flow first.
  2. Use only endpoints, zero crossings and changes in slope.
  3. For a straight net-flow segment, use change in stock = (NF_start + NF_end)/2 x elapsed time.
  4. Add each change to the previous stock value, then plot those points on a separate stock-time graph.

Behaviour rule: positive net flow means stock rises; negative means it falls; zero net flow gives a maximum, minimum or flat segment. A falling positive net flow means the stock rises at a decreasing rate.

2025/26 worked route [12]

The 2025/26 graph has outflow 50 units/day. Inflow falls from 100 to 0 over days 0-5, is zero to day 10, rises to 100 by day 15, is constant to day 20, then falls to zero by day 25. The stock starts at 100.

DayNet flowStockReason
0+50100Initial value
2.50162.5100 + 0.5 x 2.5 x 50
5-50100Equal negative triangle
10-50-150100 - 50 x 5
12.50-212.5Negative triangle
15+50-150Positive triangle

The stock peaks at day 2.5 and reaches its minimum at day 12.5. Continue the same method to day 25. A negative stock is acceptable when the paper explicitly says so.

Part (b): Euler method [5]

S(t + DT) = S(t) + Net Flow(t) x DT. Forward Euler replaces the area under the net-flow curve with a rectangle whose height is the net flow at the start of the interval.

  • Net flow is assumed constant during each time step.
  • The stock is consequently approximated as changing linearly over that step.
  • DT must be small enough for this approximation to be acceptable.

Forward Euler overestimates when net flow falls, since its left-hand rectangle is above the line. It underestimates when net flow rises. For the 2025/26 interval 0-2.5 with DT=0.5, the starting net flows are 50, 40, 30, 20 and 10, so Euler change is (50+40+30+20+10) x 0.5 = 75. The true triangle area is 0.5 x 2.5 x 50 = 62.5, hence an overestimate of 12.5 units.

Part (c): Euler table [8]

With the same 2025/26 graph and DT=5, use the start-of-interval net flow:

IntervalStarting net flowEuler updateStock
0-5+50100 + 50(5)350
5-10-50350 - 50(5)100
10-15-50100 - 50(5)-150
15-20+50-150 + 50(5)100
20-25+50100 + 50(5)350

Answer: S(25)=350. Do not use the day-25 net flow because no later interval begins there.

Mark checklist

  • Rates have units of units/time; stock has units.
  • Do not add a rate directly to a stock without multiplying by time.
  • Graphical integration uses areas; Euler uses start-of-step rectangles.
  • For every stock graph, write the behaviour mode, not only points.
